standard_prerequisites.use: Universal first order thickenings and their universal property, fibre products of algebraic spaces, and formally unramified morphisms; the verification is retained.

core_obligations: Use the universal property of the two thickenings to construct the comparison morphism between the thickening of the fibre product and the fibre product of the thickenings.
Verify the comparison is an isomorphism by testing the universal lifting property.

proof_roadmap.step: Construct the comparison morphism from the universal property.
Show the comparison satisfies the lifting property of both sides.
Conclude the comparison is an isomorphism.

difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that in a fibre product diagram of algebraic spaces with the relevant morphisms formally unramified, the universal first order thickening of the fibre product is the fibre product of the universal first order thickenings. The proof uses the universal property of the thickenings to build the comparison morphism and then checks it is an isomorphism by testing the defining lifting property on both sides. Building the comparison from the universal property and verifying it is the substantive content. Retained author proof at lines 3295-3340 with the surrounding argument.

dedup.scope: Cross-chapter same-name pair decided by the statements alone: both sides assert that the universal first order thickening commutes with the fibre product, stated for schemes on the other side and for algebraic spaces over S here. This side is the more general statement and its proof is of the same size, so under the count-the-more-general-side rule this side is counted. Compared against all focused-seeds task.json, PREPARATION_WORKLIST.jsonl, and public intervals for spaces-more-morphisms.tex.

compared.difference: Hypothesis difference: the schemes side takes the fibre product diagram in the category of schemes; this side in the category of algebraic spaces over S. Conclusion difference: none, both assert compatibility of the universal thickening with the fibre product.
